newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee treads up, cautious before holiday.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee treads up, cautious before holiday.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures edged higher by midsession on Wednesday but movements and activity were limited as players were reluctant to commit ahead of the long weekend in the United States.
The New York arabica futures market is closed on Friday for the Independence Day holiday.
Volume totalled just 871 lots. Traders said the razor-thin activity focussed on light industry buying, switches and some book-squaring.
September bucked lower opening calls to open about unchanged and ended the morning trade $5 up at $1,826, the session high. November also firmed $4 at $1,810.
July/Sept switches were traded at $28 and Sept/Nov ranged at $13-$14.

Fears of cold weather in Brazil's coffee belt that helped fuel the New York rally on Tuesday seemed to have abated. But attention is now focussed on Monday's volcanic eruption in Mexico which could force thousands of villagers to be evacuated.
The 17,890-foot (5,452-metre) giant Popocatepeti volcano, in its biggest eruption in 72 years, spewed red-hot rocks and a thick cloud ash that spread for hundreds of miles across central Mexico.
It was not immediately known if coffee farms were affected. Mexico is a key Central American producer.
Elsewhere, traders said the 574 lots of originals put up for tender on the first notice day on Tuesday was at the low end of market expectation.
But nonetheless, it was still a bit market-friendly based on the total 2,400 lots available for tenders.
A further 43 lots of originals and 42 re-tenders were posted on Wednesday.
